reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a piecewise-constant (staircase) signal with a dominant period of ~95 points, as confirmed by the estimated period and window_cycles scaling. Each cycle consists of three characteristic phases: (1) a flat plateau lasting ~30–40 points, (2) a sharp downward step (~1–2 points wide), and (3) a gradual linear descent over ~40–50 points before the next plateau. Amplitude varies across cycles (median ranges from −0.51 to +0.84 in robust standardized units), but morphology—plateau → step → ramp—is highly conserved. Peaks are flat-topped plateaus; troughs are shallow minima formed at the end of ramps, not sharp spikes. Noise is negligible: all segments are clean staircases with near-zero roughness and curvature per catalog. Minor variations exist: some cycles include tiny transient wiggles (e.g., candidate 1 at index 879–882, candidate 2 at 1840–1845), but these are sparse and low-magnitude (<0.2 std). Baseline level drifts slowly across long windows (slope_per_point ≈ ±0.0006), consistent with trend-stationarity. The 5-cycle window (candidate 3) shows the full motif repeated five times with stable phase alignment, confirming periodicity. Acceptable variation includes ±0.3 shift in median level, ±0.2 in amplitude_90, and occasional micro-wiggles ≤2 points wide; deviations beyond this—e.g., prolonged ramps, missing steps, or high-frequency jitter—are suspect.

reference_profiles.description: Single-cycle (1P) staircase: starts at −0.68, flat until index ~5, drops sharply to −0.72, stays flat to ~19, then descends linearly to −1.5 by index 89, ending with a brief flat segment and two small oscillations near the end. Very clean, no noise, minimal slope (−0.009/pt).

Three-cycle (3P) staircase with moderate baseline shift upward. Contains two minor micro-wiggles (~2 pts wide, ±0.2 amplitude) near indices 879 and 989. Plateaus are slightly shorter; ramps are smoother. Overall morphology matches consensus but with slight added variability.

Three-cycle (3P) staircase with higher baseline (median +0.84). Includes one micro-wiggle near index 1842. Ramps are slightly steeper than candidate 1; plateaus are well-defined. Morphology fully aligns with consensus; only level and minor wiggle differ.

Five-cycle (5P) staircase spanning 475 points. Shows full periodic repetition with excellent phase coherence. Contains two micro-wiggles (indices 2555, 2675), both low-amplitude and brief. Baseline drifts gently upward. Best exemplar of long-term stability and motif fidelity.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidate 3 (5P) for queries with ≥3 cycles—it provides the most robust morphological template. For single-cycle queries, use candidate 0 as primary reference due to its cleanliness; fall back to candidate 2 if baseline is elevated. Candidate 1 is acceptable but treat its micro-wiggles as potential noise—not normal—when comparing short queries. When query length matches 1P, align by cycle start (not global index); when matching 3P/5P, verify phase consistency of plateaus and step locations relative to the 95-point period.
uncertainties: Exact timing of step transitions may vary by ±2 points across normal instances; whether this is intrinsic variability or measurement artifact remains unresolved.
Micro-wiggles appear in 3/4 candidates but are sparse and low-energy; their status as normal noise vs. incipient anomaly requires query-context validation.
Baseline level shift magnitude (up to 1.35 std units across candidates) is accepted as normal trend-stationarity, but extreme shifts (>1.5 std) in queries should trigger scrutiny.
